title: Meta's Ava — a computer-use model — surfaces in closed testing inside the Meta AI desktop app
subtitle: The reveal puts Meta in the same category as ChatGPT and Claude Cowork, and ties into Project Muse — the internal Hatch super-app being repositioned for launch.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Meta is testing a computer-use model called Ava inside the Meta AI desktop app, according to Testing Catalog reporting picked up in September 3 news roundups. Ava is in closed testing, tied to the Mac app Meta shipped on August 19 that already lets users share portions of their screen for the assistant to reason over. The category — agent that can see the screen and take actions on the user's behalf — matches what ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude Cowork have shipped in public form this year.

Ava plugs into what Meta is now calling Muse, the launch brand for the agent super-app previously tracked internally as Project Hatch. Muse is the same brand as Meta's new-generation AI models, which suggests Meta wants the model, the app, and the agent surface unified under one name at market — the opposite of Google's approach of scattering Gemini across Search, Workspace, Android, and Chrome, and closer to OpenAI's single-ChatGPT strategy.

The competitive read is that Meta is trying to close the agent gap before it becomes structural. OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude both had computer-use agents in general availability by mid-2026; Google's Gemini has Antigravity and Spark; Microsoft has Agent 365. Meta's answer had been Muse Glimmer for laptops, Muse Spark for image, and the Mac app for screen-sharing — capabilities without an autonomous agent tying them together. Ava, if it ships, is that connective tissue.

For learners: watch what Ava is actually allowed to do in the release, not what the demo shows. Computer-use agents are a category where the difference between 'reads your screen and clicks buttons' and 'safely executes multi-step workflows you didn't script' is enormous. A capable one changes the surface area of software; a merely demonstrated one is a screenshot with hopes attached. The scope of allowed actions in the shipped version — file writes, purchases, message sends — is the metric that matters.
